description: Redwood Inference is building a beta “SIEM-ready audit export” capability as part of the Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation. The goal is to let enterprise customers reliably export Redwood audit events into their security tooling (initially Splunk, Datadog, and generic S3 delivery) with (1) configurable filtering, (2) delivery guarantees suitable for compliance and incident response, and (3) operational visibility. Scope includes: a canonical audit event schema (stable event_id, timestamps, actor, action, resource, tenant/workspace, source IP / user agent where applicable), an export configuration API/UI (destinations, credentials, filters, backfill window), an exporter service with at-least-once delivery (checkpointing, retries with backoff, dead-lettering), and end-to-end observability (export lag, error rates, per-destination health). Security constraints: least-privilege RBAC around export configuration, encryption in transit and at rest (including secret handling), PII minimization/redaction rules, and clear retention/backfill semantics. Rollout is gated behind feature flags and limited to a small beta cohort (hosted + dedicated first; private/on-prem considered out of scope for beta but documented for follow-on). Stakeholders: Product (Naomi Feldman) owns PRD, beta criteria, and customer selection; Security Engineering (Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei) owns audit log semantics, SIEM requirements, and threat/PII review; Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park’s org) owns configuration APIs, RBAC, and tenant isolation; Telemetry/Observability (Logan Wright’s org) owns exporter metrics and dashboards; SRE (Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes) owns SLOs, on-call readiness, and incident response. Expected phases: (1) requirements + PRD + partner/customer discovery, (2) technical design + ADRs (schema, delivery semantics, filtering model), (3) implementation across control plane + exporter + UI + IaC, (4) internal alpha with synthetic events + chaos testing, (5) limited beta with 3–5 accounts and weekly check-ins, (6) GA readiness checklist (stability, docs, security review, support playbooks).
